visuals.caption: Devices signal an interrupt controller; the controller signals the CPU.
visuals.alt: Linux Kernel Labs diagram showing several device IRQ lines entering an interrupt controller, which signals the CPU through INTR, with NMI shown separately.
visuals.learnerInference: A device driver receives a Linux IRQ abstraction above the physical interrupt-controller topology.

visuals.caption: Critical, immediate, and deferred interrupt-processing phases.
visuals.alt: Linux Kernel Labs diagram dividing interrupt processing into critical, immediate, and deferred phases, with IRQ acknowledgement and later deferred execution.
visuals.learnerInference: Substantial work should move out of the most constrained interrupt phase.

visuals.caption: Syscall, exception, and IRQ entries cross process and interrupt contexts.
visuals.alt: Linux Kernel Labs execution-context diagram showing syscalls, exceptions, IRQ entries, and returns between user mode and kernel mode.
visuals.learnerInference: Driver state is touched asynchronously from process and IRQ-related contexts and requires explicit synchronization.
